fields.harald rosemann\n\n 2020-05-07 10:57\n\n:
LaTeXDoc widely modified and restructured.
What is new:

First of all: use xelatex instead of pdflatex, call:
xelatex <report-name>.tex
to produce the desired
<report-name>.pdf.
Put this call as often as needed in succession (required
with longtable, references). xelatex will inform you, if
a rerun will be needed by sending the message:
_ Rerun LaTeX
AND if you have problems, first check: do you have
installed the latest version of tex-live full?
(For now it's texlive2019,
see: https://www.ctan.org/pkg/texlive)

Full usage of unicode utf8.
A wide range of languages and fonts are now available
e.g. those available with MS-Office are said to be usable.
(If a special glyph is missing in a font it will be blank
or replaced by the letter F in a rectangle)
Multi-language was made available by using the packages:
_ xeCJK, polyglossia, xltxtra for

chinese-japanese-korean, multi-language, additional help -.
You may change from the default settings by activating
'setmainfont...' with your choice. Three examples running
with Ubuntu are shown commented out by a leading %-character.
I had best results with 'Linux Libertine O'. Likewise
set to non-executable are some untested settings perhaps
needing an adaption. In the same way you may also activate your
favoured 'setCJKmainfont...'. In addition you may change the
'setmainlanguage...' declaration from 'english' to your choice.
For further information read the 'Package documentation' at:
https://www.ctan.org/pkg/polyglossia
and for CJK at:
https://www.ctan.org/tex-archive/fonts/CJK
_ https://www.tug.org/TUGboat/tb18-3/cjkintro600.pdf

The script is modified and restructured to a wide extent.
Smart page breaking is established and does the job in most
cases. Few exceptions are due to the preparing of data by the
main gramps document generator. This is not always done
in a consistent way. E.g. the last table 'Notes' in the
'individual report' is declared to have two columns.
In use is one column throughout overlapping both of them.
Why then a table? Furthermore the cells of the rows are
filled with large amounts of text. Since a page break can
occur at most at the end of a table-row an unpleasant early
transition to a new page is appearing. In contrast the same
text comes up in the 'detailed ancestor report' not packed
in a table. Here such blocks of text can be split over to
pages; in some cases smart page breaking is affected by the
somewhat strange construction of the delivered text.
Furthermore sometimes there is an empty paragraph before
a table start and sometimes is missing. In other cases
there is an end-of-table claimed immediately followed by
start-of-tablie in midst of a table as can be seen in the
'individual report' at the headlines 'Families' and the
second 'LDS Ordination'; as a result each with a horizontal
line shorted to the length of the headline. (All references
to gramps example person-ID: I0044, Garner von Zielinski,
Lewis Anderson)

Pictures are framed. If there is an Error in
conjunction with pictures and PIL, an error message is
propagated to <report-name>.tex to be included in the
<report-name>.pdf file and shown there instead of the
picture.

Fine tuning of vertical distances is included and mainly
concentrated in a separate class. The settings are in parts
mutual influencing. This peculiarity could have been
obsolete if text and style specifications weren't uncoupled
from their context and extruded in fragments through the
central gramps document generator (this from my LaTeX point
of view, see below).

As before there is a lot of effort in the construction
of tables. Gramps delivers them column by column made up of
cells whereas LaTeX builds tables row by row made up of
cells. In addition the column widths must be determined.
This is done in a new way by a loop controlled in python and
calculated by LaTeX.

With broader text columns there is a margin alignment.
If an hyphenation should be false or isn't wanted, the user
may interfere by means of the file 'mapping.csv' in his
working directory. If it is missing, it will automatically
be invoked with some lines commented out to show in short
the usage. In two columns a mapping may be provided for
gramps terms to be replaced by LaTeX phrases. Thus
hyphenation patterns can be modified or transcriptions are
made possible. The file may be edited by the user with any
spreadsheet program.

Further Remarks:
This script seems to be complicated. Yes, it is. This is
due to the packing of data in small generalized packages
by the central gramps document generator, which must be
interpreted and assigned to LaTeX entities without knowing
about their significance with respect to the special report.
If from the beginning you are aware of what should be
displayed, the things could be very simple.

E.g. the 'record report' could use the 'enumerate' scheme,
a special list structure of LaTeX. The python script
could look like:

for recordtype in <list of record types>:
write_tex(<recordtype>)
writetex('\begin{enumerate}')
for placement_data in <list of placement data of recordtype>:
writetex('\item')
write_tex(placementdata)
writetex('\end{enumerate}')

Add the LaTeX declarations - no '\newcommand' is needed -
add furthermore the Title and if wanted some styles as well
as space adjustments and you are done.

In a similar manner you could use the 'description' scheme
instead with 'item[<place number>]'; 'description' could
also be applied to some other reports and in a nested form
to the 'descend report'. Far more convenient might be the
usage of the generalised list structure to be tailored to
the wanted special requirements and conceptions in each
case.

To carry on the considerations: Table setup could be
more clear and efficient, whereby adapted to the special
content. From the beginning should be known precisely,
what to display in which number of columns. And not always
there is a table needed. E.g. a picture could be placed as
block side by side to other blocks much like letters are
lined up to words, words to lines which for their part may
be followed by further lines. Or even better: pictures could
be placed on positions free to choose by the
LaTeX-environment 'picture'.

Yes things could be far more simple, much more clear,
But here we are bound to the central gramps document
generator and its preparations.

~

calculated by LaTeX.

With broader text columns there is a margin alignment.
If an hyphenation should be false or isn't wanted, the user
may interfere by means of the file 'mapping.csv' in his
working directory. If it is missing, it will automatically
be invoked with some lines commented out to show in short
the usage. In two columns a mapping may be provided for
gramps terms to be replaced by LaTeX phrases. Thus
hyphenation patterns can be modified or transcriptions are
made possible. The file may be edited by the user with any
spreadsheet program.

Further Remarks:
This script seems to be complicated. Yes, it is. This is
due to the packing of data in small generalized packages
by the central gramps document generator, which must be
interpreted and assigned to LaTeX entities without knowing
about their significance with respect to the special report.
If from the beginning you are aware of what should be
displayed, the things could be very simple.

E.g. the 'record report' could use the 'enumerate' scheme,
a special list structure of LaTeX. The python script
could look like:

for recordtype in <list of record types>:
write_tex(<recordtype>)
writetex('\begin{enumerate}')
for placement_data in <list of placement data of recordtype>:
writetex('\item')
write_tex(placementdata)
writetex('\end{enumerate}')

Add the LaTeX declarations - no '\newcommand' is needed -
add furthermore the Title and if wanted some styles as well
as space adjustments and you are done.

In a similar manner you could use the 'description' scheme
instead with 'item[<place number>]'; 'description' could
also be applied to some other reports and in a nested form
to the 'descend report'. Far more convenient might be the
usage of the generalised list structure to be tailored to
the wanted special requirements and conceptions in each
case.

To carry on the considerations: Table setup could be
more clear and efficient, whereby adapted to the special
content. From the beginning should be known precisely,
what to display in which number of columns. And not always
there is a table needed. E.g. a picture could be placed as
block side by side to other blocks much like letters are
lined up to words, words to lines which for their part may
be followed by further lines. Or even better: pictures could
be placed on positions free to choose by the
LaTeX-environment 'picture'.

Yes things could be far more simple, much more clear,
But here we are bound to the central gramps document
generator and its preparations.

~
